harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (rabbitmq-server 3.12.1 on Ubuntu 24.04) across node1/node2/node3, serving AMQP over TLS on 5671 with a dedicated cluster CA. The AMQP listener requires verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert, so only clients presenting a certificate issued by that CA can connect (verified: valid cert -> handshake succeeds and AMQP login/publish/consume works; no cert -> certificate-required alert; cert from a foreign CA -> Bad Certificate alert). The management UI (15672) is bound only to each node's private cluster IP and additionally firewalled via iptables/netfilter-persistent to accept only the three cluster node IPs, dropping all other sources; verified reachable (401 on bad creds) from cluster peers. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/queue health, issued native reboot, polled until the node was reachable again, proved boot_id changed on each, and confirmed RabbitMQ auto-started, rejoined the cluster (3/3 running nodes), firewall rules persisted, and TLS client-cert enforcement plus end-to-end AMQPS messaging still worked after each restart, waiting for full cluster health before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Installed rabbitmq-server + Erlang and enabled rabbitmq_management plugin on node1, node2, node3
Populated /etc/hosts with cluster hostnames and generated/distributed a shared Erlang cookie (via secret_env) to enable clustering
Created a dedicated cluster CA on node1 (openssl), issued per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+IP) and one client certificate, all signed by that CA

Distributed CA cert and node-specific server cert/key to node2/node3 via a temporary HTTP file server (no SSH available between nodes), then shut the server down and locked file permissions to the rabbitmq user

Configured /etc/rabbitmq/rabbitmq.conf on each node: TLS-only AMQP listener (listeners.tcp=none, listeners.ssl.default=5671) with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, management.tcp.ip bound to the node's private IP, and classic_config cluster_formation peer list
Started rabbitmq-server on all nodes and joined node2/node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster
Created an appuser administrator account with a generated password and deleted the default guest user
Added iptables rules (persisted via iptables-persistent/netfilter-persistent) on each node to allow management port 15672 only from the three cluster node IPs and drop all other sources

Verified TLS enforcement with openssl s_client: valid CA-issued client cert succeeds, no client cert yields a certificate-required alert, and a cert from an unrelated self-signed CA yields a Bad Certificate alert (checked against RabbitMQ logs)
Verified end-to-end AMQPS connectivity/messaging via a Python pika client using the CA-issued client cert against all three broker IPs
Verified management API is reachable (401 on bad creds, not connection-refused) from within the cluster network on each node's bound IP

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id and health baseline, rebooted node1 then node2 then node3 one at a time via native `sudo reboot`, polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified cluster membership (3/3 running), firewall persistence, TLS client-cert enforcement, and AMQPS messaging after each restart before proceeding to the next node

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all three rabbit@node1/2/3 as both Disk Nodes and Running Nodes after join_cluster on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Dedicated CA created for the cluster and used to sign server + client certs
evidence.summary: openssl generated ca-key.pem/ca-cert.pem; per-node server certs and one client cert were signed by this CA and openssl verify confirmed both server (node1) and client certs chain to it

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS on all nodes
evidence.summary: cluster_status lists amqp/ssl on port 5671 as the only AMQP listener; ss -tlnp confirms only 5671 (ssl) is listening on each node, no plaintext 5672

evidence.requirement: Only clients presenting a CA-issued certificate are accepted for AMQP
evidence.summary: openssl s_client + rabbitmq log show valid CA-signed client cert succeeds, no cert triggers 'certificate required' fatal alert, and a foreign self-signed cert triggers 'Bad Certificate' fatal alert; pika end-to-end test using the CA-issued client cert publishes/consumes successfully against all 3 nodes, both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip binds 15672 only to each node's private cluster IP (ss -tlnp), and iptables rules accept only the 3 cluster node IPs on 15672 and DROP everything else; curl from node2 and node1 to the management API returns 401 (reachable, auth-gated) confirming intra-cluster reachability

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data/firewall state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bfd05127... captured pre-reboot; reboot ack returned before disconnect (subsequent poll got connection reset/timeout); post-reboot boot_id bf8463cc... proves an actual restart; rabbitmq-server auto-active, node2's log shows 'rabbit on node rabbit@node1 up', and iptables 15672 rules still present after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data/firewall state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id cf34dc87... captured pre-reboot; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id f499ebdc... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running with iptables 15672 rules intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/data/firewall state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 63f96994... captured pre-reboot; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 1af46fc6... confirms restart; rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running with iptables 15672 rules intact
